original_question: In which domain of the voltage-gated potassium channel encoded by the KCNQ2 gene are the R207W and R214W mutations located, which lead to altered channel gating kinetics in benign familial neonatal seizures (BFNS)?

final_qi.question: In which domain of the voltage-gated potassium channel encoded by the KCNQ2 gene are the R207W and R214W mutations located, which lead to altered channel gating kinetics in benign familial neonatal seizures (BFNS)?
final_qi.long_answer: The R207W and R214W substitutions both lie in the S4 transmembrane segment of Kv7.2, the positively charged voltage-sensor domain that detects membrane potential changes; altering these arginines disrupts normal gating kinetics and causes BFNS.

0.question: What are the R207W and R214W mutations in the KCNQ2 gene associated with?

final_answer.long_answer: Residues Arg207 and Arg214 lie within the fourth trans-membrane segment (S4) of KCNQ2. S4 is the positively charged voltage-sensing segment of Kv7.2; mutations here (R207W, R214W) disturb the movement of this sensor, slowing activation and speeding deactivation, which alters channel gating kinetics observed in benign familial neonatal seizures.
